SPECIFICATION FOR CALORIMETER THERMOMETERS
PART 1 SOLID-STEM THERMOMETERS

Prescribes the requirements for a series of short-range solid-stem calorimeter thermometers 1. Scopegraduated for vertical, total and partial immersion, for use in bomb calorimetry and other purpose4 Jvhere an accurate measurement of a change of temperature is required.

On partial immersion thermometers, a line shall be etched at least half way round the stem of the thermometer at the level to which it is intended to be immersed. 5. Requirements 5.1 Materials bulb shall be made of suitable thermometric glass (see IS : 4610-1968 5.1 .l Glass -Thermometer Specification for glass tubes for general purposes and reference thermometers ). The glass or glasses comprising the thermometer shall be so selected and processed that the finished thermometer shows the following characteristics: a) Stress in the glass shall be reduced to a level sufficient due to thermal or mechanical shock: to minimize the possibility of fracture

b) The correction of the thermometer reading at the lowest temperature of the nominal range shall not change by more than 0*02'C immediately after the thermometer has been heated for 15 min at a temperature 30�C higher than the lowest temperature and allowed to cool naturally in air; c) The legibility d) The meniscus 5.1.2 Thermometric gases. of the reading shall not be impaired by devitrification shall not be distorted by defects or impurities liquid or clouding;

5.2.5 Contraction chamber - A contraction chamber shall be provided so that the mercury does not recede into the bulb at 0�C. 6.2 The scale lines shall be clearly etched and of uniform thickness, which exceed 0'05 mm. The lines shall be at right angles to the axis of the thermometer.

in

no

case

shall

6.3 When the thermometer is held in a vertical position and viewed from the front, the left-hand ends of all the scale lines shall lie on an imaginary vertical line. When the thermometer is viewed so that the right-hand ends of the shorter lines, denoting an interval of O.Ol"C, align with the left-hand size of the bore, longer lines at each 0'05�C shall extend across the bore towards the right. The shorter lines shall be about 1 mm long.
6.4 The figures shall be placed in such a way that an extension of the line to which they refer would They may be placed either to the left or to the right of the scale lines, as preferred.

bisect them.

6.5 The scale lines shall be so positioned that the enamel backing in the stem provides a background for the figures, the scale and the mercury column when the latter is seen just beyond the left or right hand ends of the short lines ( see Fig. 2 ).

7.1 Scale Error-The scale error, when the thermometer is under when the emergent liquid column ( in the case of a partial immersion temperature, shall not be greater than O*l"C.

calorimeter thermometers', issued by the

The calorimeter thermometers are not provided with auxiliary scales at O'C and are, therefore, not suited to the absolute measurement of temperature, unless they are checked against a standard are covered in Part 2 of this thermometer immediate before use.
